newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam, Thailand "deadlocked" on overlapping seas.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam, Thailand "deadlocked" on overlapping seas.

text.p: Vietnam and Thailand failed to make progress on a dispute over overlapping maritime territory during a 24-hour visit to Hanoi by Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, diplomats said on Monday.

A long-running argument over competing claims in the Gulf of Thailand, where the Thai and Vietnamese continental shelves overlap for about 6,000 sq km (2,300 sq miles), was only mentioned briefly during Chavalit's talks, they said.
"It's deadlock," said one Thai diplomat. "We have had seven rounds of talks between technicians. What we need now is a political decision from both countries."
The two sides will hold further technical talks in May on a joint development area or even joint ventures for fishing in the contested area.
Relations between the two countries have warmed considerably since Vietnam joined the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in 1995.
However, the maritime sovereignty dispute has remained a problem and fishermen from the two countries have in the past clashed or been detained in the overlapping areas.
No fishermen are currently being held on either side, although Thailand says Vietnam is still holding 18 fishing vessels which it wants returned.
Diplomats said Chavalit had come to Hanoi with Thailand's formal position on a South China Sea sovereignty row between Vietnam and China prepared in advance.

Thailand has taken no side in the dispute and believes that talks should be held to find a solution. However, diplomats said that neither Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet nor Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi raised the subject up during talks.

"As a partner in ASEAN, we had expected something on this. But neither side brought it up," said one Thai diplomat, noting ASEAN countries' natural aversion to controversy. ASEAN groups Indonesia, Singapore, Malaysia, Philippines, Brunei, Thailand and Vietnam.
"It's good that the Vietnamese didn't mention it because our relations with China are pretty good right now," he added.
Vietnam is hoping to hold talks with China this week on competing claims to an offshore area where a Chinese oil rig has been drilling, Vietnamese Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam said on Monday.

The two communist neighbours have competing claims on areas along their land border, on parts of the Tonkin Gulf and on the Paracel Island chain, which lies east of the latest area of dispute. They are also among six regional claimants to the Spratly Islands, which are farther south.
Chavalit is due to leave for a four-day visit to China on Tuesday, during which he is expected to seek closer ties between the two nations' armed forces and boost trade.
Business also appeared to be high on Chavalit's agenda during his brief trip to Hanoi.

He told a news conference on Sunday that Kiet had agreed to ease the way for Thailand to open more bank branches in Vietnam and the two sides agreed to increase the number of flights between Bangkok and Ho Chi Minh City to nine a week from seven.
Chavalit also witnessed the signing ceremony for a $237.8 million cement venture between Thailand's SAS Trading Company Limited and Vietnam's Mine and Engineering Company.
Thailand ranks 19th among foreign investors in Vietnam, so far committing about $1.2 billion for 74 projects. Two-way trade amounted to $610 million in 1996.
